exposure: Vaginal misoprostol combined with a Foley balloon for labor induction
Vaginal misoprostol alone for labor induction
outcome: Satisfaction rates regarding the duration of labor induction
cohort: The study involved singleton full-term pregnant women with fetuses in the cephalic position, divided into a combination group (n=94) and a misoprostol alone group (n=105).
finding: Vaginal misoprostol combined with a Foley balloon significantly shortens the induction-to-delivery time but causes more severe pain during labor induction, leading to overall maternal satisfaction comparable to vaginal misoprostol alone.
mod_finding: The benefit of a shorter induction-to-delivery time with the combination method was still observed when analyses included only women with vaginal births.
